network.overall_strategy: Parallel literature-supported routes are encoded rather than a single one-pot scenario. Pyruvate is used as the main hub because pyruvate-to-alanine is the best-supported experimental transformation; two hydrothermal C3-source modules feed four pyruvate-to-rac-alanine modules, giving eight pathways. Classical Strecker chemistry and a thiol-assisted formose/aldehyde route provide two independent surface alternatives. All feedstock routes produce rac-alanine, so a final explicit, weakly supported surface enantioenrichment module is included to reach L-alanine; lactate competition is acknowledged in the pyruvate-amination reasoning rather than expanded as a separate node.

reactions.name: Mineral-assisted CO2/H2 fixation to pyruvate

conditions.other: alkaline, H2-rich vent fluid; pyruvate observed at only micromolar levels

reactions.mechanism: Surface-mediated CO2 reduction to C1/C2 species followed by mineral-promoted C-C coupling to the alpha-keto acid.
reactions.reasoning: Preiner et al. (2020) detected pyruvate, along with formate and acetate, from CO2/H2 on greigite, magnetite, and awaruite under alkaline hydrothermal conditions. Amend and Shock (1998) also showed that amino-acid synthesis is thermodynamically favored in H2-rich hydrothermal systems. The main limitation is yield: pyruvate is only a low-abundance product, so this node is treated as the upstream bottleneck rather than assumed to supply concentrated pyruvate.

reactions.name: NiS-mediated acetylene/CO synthesis of pyruvate

conditions.other: CO-rich hydrothermal setting; short residence times favored because pyruvate is thermally fragile

reactions.mechanism: NiS-bound acetylene undergoes carbonylation and hydration to give the C3 alpha-keto acid.
reactions.reasoning: Huber et al. (2020) reported pyruvate formation from acetylene and CO on NiS at temperatures above 100 C. This route can bypass the very low yields of direct CO2/H2 pyruvate formation, but it inherits the thermal-fragility critique for pyruvate and amino acids at elevated temperature emphasized by Miller and Bada (1988).

reactions.name: Green-rust reductive amination of pyruvate

conditions.other: pH about 10, Fe(II):Fe(III) about 1:1, high NH3 activity; lactate competes strongly at lower pH

reactions.mechanism: Pyruvate first forms an imine or iminopyruvate with ammonia, then the surface provides the reducing equivalents needed to hydrogenate the C=N intermediate to alanine.
reactions.reasoning: Barge et al. (2019) found the strongest alanine selectivity in mixed-valence iron hydroxides, with about 70% alanine at pH 10 and 70 C and much higher lactate production at lower pH or less favorable redox state. Their laboratory system likely used the mineral as the immediate reductant, so representing the step with H2 is an explicit geochemical abstraction that captures vent reducing power while preserving elemental balance.

reactions.name: Electroreduced FeS reductive amination of pyruvate

conditions.other: pH 9.6, about 0.5 M NH3, sustained negative potential analogous to alkaline vent redox gradients

reactions.mechanism: Ammonia forms an imine with pyruvate and the reduced FeS surface supplies electrons for reductive amination.
reactions.reasoning: Kitadai et al. (2019) showed that electroreduced FeS converted pyruvate to alanine nearly completely within 48 h at pH 9.6 with high ammonia. The experimentally critical driver is a sustained negative potential; H2 is included here only as the balanced thermodynamic equivalent of that reducing power. The geochemical availability of such persistent potentials remains an open systems question.

reactions.name: Ni0/H2 reductive amination of pyruvate

conditions.other: pH 7-8; useful conversion even at millimolar NH3; lactate remains a side product

reactions.mechanism: Nickel catalyzes hydrogenation of the pyruvate-derived imine or iminopyruvate to alanine.
reactions.reasoning: Kaur et al. (2024) reported 18-40% alanine from pyruvate under H2 with Ni catalysts and still appreciable conversion at about 6 mM NH3, relaxing the high-ammonia critique of older Fe-mineral systems. This is the cleanest experimentally supported balanced pyruvate-to-alanine route in the network, although native Ni availability and sustained H2 pressure are still caveats.

reactions.name: Bucherer-Bergs cyclization of pyruvate to 5-methylhydantoin

conditions.other: cyanide/ammonia aqueous pool with dissolved CO2/HCO3- present and mechanistically essential, though not net consumed in this simplified step

reactions.mechanism: Cyanide adds to the keto acid and the resulting adduct cyclizes through Bucherer-Bergs chemistry to the hydantoin.
reactions.reasoning: Pulletikurti et al. (2022) showed that alpha-ketoacids react with cyanide and ammonia sources through Bucherer-Bergs chemistry to hydantoin or N-carbamoyl intermediates en route to alpha-amino acids. Their study and the associated discussion identified dissolved CO2 as mechanistically essential, so CO2 is treated here as an indispensable condition even though the simplified balanced step does not consume it net.

reactions.name: Hydantoin hydrolysis to alanine

conditions.other: mild aqueous hydrolysis of the hydantoin pool

reactions.mechanism: Ring opening and hydrolysis of the hydantoin release alanine together with CO2 and NH3.
reactions.reasoning: This is the downstream hydrolysis step of the Bucherer-Bergs pathway documented by Pulletikurti et al. (2022). It is chemically important because it links a cyanide-enabled route to a metabolic carbon skeleton, but it still requires pyruvate and cyanide to become co-localized in the same aqueous setting.

reactions.name: Strecker aminonitrile formation from acetaldehyde

conditions.other: HCN- and aldehyde-rich aqueous surface setting; compatible with spark-discharge or cyanosulfidic feedstock supply

reactions.mechanism: Acetaldehyde forms an imine with ammonia and cyanide adds to that imine to generate the alpha-aminonitrile.
reactions.reasoning: This is the canonical first half of Strecker synthesis. Prebiotic settings that supply acetaldehyde and HCN include spark-discharge chemistry (Miller, 1953; Parker et al., 2011; Cleaves et al., 2008) and cyanosulfidic surface networks (Patel et al., 2015). Encoding the aminonitrile explicitly avoids overcompressing the Strecker route and keeps the mass balance correct.

reactions.name: Aminopropionitrile hydrolysis to alanine

conditions.other: neutral to mildly alkaline hydrolysis; low NH3 or low pH would favor cyanohydrin/lactate side chemistry

reactions.mechanism: The nitrile hydrates stepwise through amide chemistry to the amino acid, liberating ammonia overall.
reactions.reasoning: Aminonitrile hydrolysis is the canonical second half of Strecker synthesis and is supported both by classical chemistry and by isotope evidence linking meteoritic alanine to Strecker-like formation (Chimiak et al., 2022). Patel et al. (2015) and later cyanosulfidic work also emphasize that aminonitrile versus cyanohydrin partitioning is sensitive to ammonia activity and pH, which is why neutral-to-alkaline conditions are favored here.

reactions.name: Thiol-assisted formose/aldehyde synthesis of alanine

conditions.other: pH about 5.2, weeks-long reaction, low yield

reactions.mechanism: Formose-derived carbonyls pass through glyceraldehyde or methylglyoxal-like intermediates, thiol capture, and imine chemistry before hydrolysis gives alanine.
reactions.reasoning: Weber (1985) and Weber (1998) obtained alanine from glyceraldehyde or from formaldehyde plus glycolaldehyde plus NH3 in water only when a thiol catalyst was present; the route is real but slow and low yielding. Related aldehyde-ammonia chemistry also appears in parent-body aqueous systems (Kebukawa et al., 2017; Koga and Naraoka, 2017). This node is therefore included as a cyanide-free alternative, with the low yield and the prebiotic availability of the organic thiol explicitly acknowledged as weaknesses.

reactions.name: Surface enantioenrichment to L-alanine

conditions.other: dry film or evaporative residue under far-UV circularly polarized irradiation, followed by repeated wet-dry recrystallization; only small ee is experimentally demonstrated

reactions.mechanism: Asymmetric photolysis or photochemistry creates a small enantiomeric excess that is then hypothetically amplified by selective recrystallization or related physical sorting.
reactions.reasoning: No published prebiotic synthesis makes alanine with substantial L-selectivity; alanine in meteorites is generally racemic and the earlier Murchison L-excess claim is disputed (Pizzarello and Cronin, 1998; Glavin et al., 2021; Glavin et al., 2025). Circularly polarized UV gives only percent-level alanine enantiomeric excess (Meinert et al., 2014; Modica et al., 2014), so this node is explicitly speculative and represents a small asymmetric bias plus unresolved amplification rather than a demonstrated high-yield synthetic step.

pathways.name: CO2/H2 fixation plus green-rust amination
pathways.description: Hydrothermal CO2/H2 fixation first makes pyruvate, green rust aminates it to rac-alanine, and a speculative surface enrichment module then biases the product toward L-alanine.

pathways.name: CO2/H2 fixation plus electroreduced FeS amination
pathways.description: Hydrothermal CO2/H2 fixation makes pyruvate, electroreduced FeS converts it to rac-alanine under alkaline vent-like redox conditions, and surface enrichment supplies the L bias.

pathways.name: CO2/H2 fixation plus Ni/H2 amination
pathways.description: Pyruvate produced from CO2/H2 is aminated on native nickel under H2 and then enters the common surface enrichment step to reach L-alanine.

pathways.name: CO2/H2 fixation plus Bucherer-Bergs bridge route
pathways.description: Hydrothermal CO2/H2 chemistry supplies pyruvate, which is trapped in a cyanide-bearing prebiotic pool as a hydantoin and hydrolyzed to rac-alanine before speculative surface enrichment.

pathways.name: Acetylene/CO pyruvate route plus green-rust amination
pathways.description: NiS-mediated hydrothermal acetylene/CO chemistry furnishes pyruvate, green rust converts it to rac-alanine, and surface enrichment biases the product toward L-alanine.

pathways.name: Acetylene/CO pyruvate route plus electroreduced FeS amination
pathways.description: A NiS hydrothermal route generates pyruvate, electroreduced FeS aminates it under alkaline reducing conditions, and a later surface step provides the only encoded L bias.

pathways.name: Acetylene/CO pyruvate route plus Ni/H2 amination
pathways.description: Hydrothermal acetylene/CO chemistry yields pyruvate and H2, native nickel uses the reducing environment to give rac-alanine, and surface enrichment gives the target enantiomer.

pathways.name: Acetylene/CO pyruvate route plus Bucherer-Bergs bridge route
pathways.description: Pyruvate from NiS-mediated acetylene/CO chemistry enters a cyanide/ammonia hydantoin pathway and is then hydrolyzed to rac-alanine before speculative surface enrichment.

pathways.name: Surface Strecker route via aminopropionitrile
pathways.description: Acetaldehyde, HCN, and NH3 form aminopropionitrile in a Strecker step, hydrolysis gives rac-alanine, and a final surface enrichment module provides L-alanine.

pathways.name: Thiol-assisted formose/aldehyde route
pathways.description: Formaldehyde and glycolaldehyde react with ammonia in a thiol-assisted surface network to give rac-alanine directly, which then undergoes speculative surface enantioenrichment.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Coherent hydrothermal route to rac-alanine, and green-rust amination is experimentally supported. Main weaknesses are the micromolar pyruvate output and missing mineral identity in rxn_001, the use of H2 instead of explicitly redox-active green rust in rxn_003, and the very weakly supported final enantioenrichment.
suggestions: Write rxn_001 with corrected coefficients 3 CO2 + 5 H2 -> pyruvate + 3 H2O and state the mineral plus realistic concentration regime.
Recast rxn_003 around mixed-valence green rust at alkaline pH and high NH3, or explicitly justify H2 as the electron source.
Model rxn_011 as partial ee or resolution with an explicit surface mechanism and transport from hydrothermal fluids.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Electroreduced FeS amination is one of the strongest pyruvate-to-alanine modules, but the pathway still inherits the dilute CO2/H2 pyruvate source and does not encode the required negative potential or pre-reduced FeS surface. The final L step remains unsupported.
suggestions: Keep the corrected stoichiometry for rxn_001 and add a concentrating mechanism for micromolar pyruvate.
Specify the required negative potential or pre-electroreduced FeS state for rxn_004.
Replace the full rac-alanine to L-alanine conversion in rxn_011 with a small-ee enrichment or resolution step.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This is the strongest of the CO2/H2-fed hydrothermal variants because Ni/H2 reductive amination is well matched to the written chemistry. Confidence is still limited by low pyruvate supply, the need for Ni and elevated H2 pressure, and the unsupported racemate to L conversion.
suggestions: State the corrected stoichiometry and likely mineral context for rxn_001.
Annotate rxn_005 with Ni source, pH, NH3 loading, and H2 pressure.
Add an explicit surface export and partial enantioenrichment mechanism instead of a complete stereo-conversion.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: The pyruvate to hydantoin to alanine bridge is literature-backed, but the implementation misses the experimentally essential CO2 or bicarbonate context for Bucherer-Bergs and rxn_007 needs 2 H2O stoichiometrically. The Biochemical label is not a clear prebiotic environment, and the final L step is weak.
suggestions: Add CO2 or bicarbonate as an essential condition for rxn_006 and replace the Biochemical label with an actual aqueous environment.
Correct rxn_007 to hydantoin + 2 H2O -> alanine + CO2 + NH3.
Do not treat rxn_011 as full conversion to L-alanine unless a credible chiral selection mechanism is specified.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Acetylene/CO to pyruvate avoids the very dilute CO2 fixation module, but it needs explicit NiS and temperature control, after which the same green-rust issues from P1 remain. Surface enantioenrichment is again the limiting step.
suggestions: Write rxn_002 with corrected stoichiometry C2H2 + CO + 2 H2O -> pyruvate + H2 and specify NiS plus temperature window.
Recast rxn_003 with green-rust redox chemistry and realistic NH3 and pH conditions.
Add a transport and concentration step before any surface enantioenrichment.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Chemically reasonable modular route: NiS-mediated pyruvate formation followed by electroreduced FeS amination has literature precedents. The missing electrochemical conditions, lack of an explicit transfer to surface, and unsupported L enrichment hold the score down.
suggestions: Correct rxn_002 stoichiometry and specify the NiS hydrothermal context.
Encode the electrochemical requirements of rxn_004 rather than only naming electroreduced FeS.
Replace rxn_011 with an explicit partial ee mechanism.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Probably the strongest hydrothermal chain in the network: both the NiS acetylene/CO pyruvate step and Ni/H2 amination have experimental support. It still needs explicit NiS and 5 bar scale H2 conditions and does not solve the final L-alanine problem.
suggestions: Correct rxn_002 stoichiometry and define the NiS temperature and residence time assumptions.
Annotate rxn_005 with realistic H2 pressure, Ni source, pH, and NH3 concentration.
Treat enantioenrichment as a separate low-yield surface selection step, not complete conversion.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: A plausible bridge route on paper, but the Bucherer-Bergs step needs CO2 or bicarbonate in the conditions and the hydrolysis stoichiometry should be corrected. The route also jumps from hot hydrothermal pyruvate generation to a vague Biochemical module and then to surface enantioenrichment without transport justification.
suggestions: Correct rxn_002 stoichiometry and specify the NiS hydrothermal conditions.
State the CO2 or bicarbonate requirement for rxn_006 and correct rxn_007 to use 2 H2O.
Make the transfer from hydrothermal to surface settings explicit and weaken rxn_011 to partial enrichment.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Best-aligned pathway. Classical Strecker formation of alpha-aminopropionitrile and subsequent hydrolysis to alanine are robust literature chemistry and fit a surface aqueous setting. The remaining weakness is that rxn_009 should consume 2 H2O and the final step does not yet provide a credible route from rac-alanine to L-alanine.
suggestions: Correct rxn_009 to aminopropionitrile + 2 H2O -> alanine + NH3 and specify hydrolysis conditions.
If desired, add an upstream HCN or acetaldehyde generation module instead of treating both as unrestricted starts.
Replace rxn_011 with a quantified small-ee enrichment or resolution mechanism.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Weber-type aldehyde chemistry is real but low-yield, slow, and thiol-dependent. Because the named thiol catalyst is not represented and the final enantioenrichment is still speculative, this route is weaker than the Strecker module.
suggestions: Add the thiol catalyst explicitly to rxn_010 or at least annotate it as an essential condition.
State the low-yield, long-time, mildly acidic conditions for the Weber route.
Model the last step as partial enantioenrichment rather than complete conversion to L-alanine.

evaluation.network_feedback: Connected and mostly internally consistent network: RDKit reports 0 unbalanceable reactions, but rxn_001 should be 3 CO2 + 5 H2 -> pyruvate + 3 H2O, rxn_002 should be C2H2 + CO + 2 H2O -> pyruvate + H2, and rxn_007 and rxn_009 each need 2 H2O; mol_010 also needs a repairable structure or InChI. Literature alignment is good for the rac-alanine chemistry: Strecker, pyruvate reductive amination, Bucherer-Bergs, and Weber-style aldehyde chemistry are all represented and the network explicitly notes lactate competition, low pyruvate supply, and the chirality bottleneck. The main reason confidence stays moderate is rxn_011; current literature does not support a robust prebiotic full conversion of rac-alanine to L-alanine, only weak or contested small-ee scenarios. Additional issues are the missing CO2 or bicarbonate context for rxn_006, omission of the thiol catalyst in rxn_010, and lack of explicit transport and concentration steps from hydrothermal modules to a surface enrichment setting. Best current pathway is P9, but overall this is a strong modular rac-alanine network rather than a demonstrated L-alanine synthesis network, so it is not approved.
